label: Authority claim
definition: The sender presents as an institution or person with power over the recipient (bank, employer, school, government office, landlord) to make the request seem legitimate.

label: Urgency pressure
definition: The message imposes a deadline or immediate consequence so the recipient acts before checking.

label: Fear
definition: The message threatens a loss or penalty, such as account suspension, disconnection, a fine or a child being sent home.

label: Sympathy appeal
definition: The sender invokes hardship, an emergency or a personal mistake to elicit help.

label: Reward bait
definition: The message offers a prize, bonus, airtime, points or another unearned benefit.

label: Opportunity bait
definition: The message offers a job, placement, scholarship or similar opportunity the recipient did not seek.

label: Income promise
definition: The message promises easy or guaranteed earnings, typically for little effort.

label: High-return promise
definition: The message promises investment returns well above normal market rates or guaranteed returns.

label: Advance fee
definition: The recipient must pay a fee, deposit or charge before receiving a promised benefit.

label: Payment redirection
definition: The message asks the recipient to send an expected payment to a new or different account, number or paybill.

label: Reversal pretext
definition: The sender claims a transaction went wrong and asks for funds to be returned or resent.

label: Exclusivity
definition: The recipient is told they were specially selected or that payment must go only through a stated channel.

label: Scarcity
definition: The message claims limited slots, stock or availability to force a quick decision.

label: Social proof
definition: The message cites other people's participation or success to build credibility.

label: Familiarity
definition: The sender poses as someone the recipient already knows, such as a friend, relative or contact on a new number.

label: Trust exploitation
definition: The message abuses an existing trusted relationship or channel, such as a known contact's real account.

label: Trust appeal
definition: The message uses reassurance or trust signals (official-sounding language, guarantees) to lower suspicion.

label: Curiosity
definition: The message withholds information (results, a parcel, a message) to prompt the recipient to click or respond.

label: Suspicious link
definition: The message contains a link with a lookalike domain, odd characters or no clear relation to the claimed sender.

label: Shortened URL
definition: The message uses a URL shortener that hides the true destination.

label: Compromised account
definition: The message is sent from a genuine account (e.g. WhatsApp) that has been taken over by the scammer.

label: Religious appeal
definition: The message invokes God, scripture, prayer or a church to build trust or apply moral pressure.
